mainTopic: כלאים in a small garden bed: רב's precaution about the corners, שמואל's bed among beds, a single furrow as a separator, and רבי יוחנן's five-circle method with the debate over the spaces between
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's discussion of the משנה that lets a person plant five kinds of seeds in a 6x6 טפחים garden bed. First the גמרא explains that רב's restriction is a גזירה, a precaution in case the person also fills the corners. It answers that the ראש תור leniency, for a triangle-shaped tip of one field poking into another, does not help in a small bed. שמואל rules that the משנה applies even to a bed surrounded by other beds, as long as the rows face different directions. עולא then reports a question from ארץ ישראל: does one furrow count as a separation? רב ששת says no and רב אסי says yes. The lenient view survives a challenge from single rows of cucumbers, gourds and beans, because those plants spread tangling branches. Next רבי יוחנן teaches how to fill a whole garden: make a 6x6 bed with five circles and plant the corners. The school of רבי ינאי says the spaces between the circles stay empty, while רב אשי lets them be planted in the opposite direction. רבינא begins a challenge to רב אשי from a ברייתא about six טפחים of work space, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב's reason: a precaution in case he fills the corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב's ruling as a גזירה, a protective decree, in case the person goes on to plant in the corners of the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he will fill the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving its final explanation of רב's reason. רב's restriction exists because the person might later plant in the corners of the bed, and that could create forbidden כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier explanations of רב were apparently not accepted, so the גמרא now says רב's rule is a precaution. It is not forbidden in itself. The rabbis worried that a person who plants this way will also fill the corners, and then the different species would be too close together.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic precaution, a fence made to stop a person from reaching a real prohibition
The prohibition of planting different species together

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a discussion. The line 'גזירה שמא ימלא את הקרנות' is the גמרא's explanation of רב's earlier statement, which is not quoted here. It is not a brand-new topic.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he will fill the corners.
phrases.notes: This is the reason behind רב's ruling, which was discussed on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier by giving the reason for רב's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason: רב's rule is a rabbinic precaution, not a direct prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's restriction is a גזירה in case the person fills the corners of the bed.

steps.title: Challenge: filling the corners should be allowed like a triangular plot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why filling the corners is a problem at all. It should be like ראש תור, a triangle-shaped tip of one field poking into another, which a משנה permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it be no worse than a triangular tip of vegetables! Didn't we learn in a משנה: If a triangular tip of vegetables was poking into another field, it is permitted, because you can see where the field ends?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given. Even if the person fills the corners, why should that be forbidden? A משנה permits a triangle-shaped tip of one field to poke into another field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of ראש תור, the triangle shape makes it obvious where one field ends and the other begins, so there is no forbidden mix. The corners of a square bed also make a kind of point. So the corners should be permitted too, and then there is nothing to make a precaution about.

keyTerms.meaning: A triangle-shaped tip of one field that pokes into another field
Didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a challenge from a משנה)
The end of the field can be seen, so the border is clear

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא רֹאשׁ תּוֹר יָרָק?
phrases.english: But let it be no worse than a triangular tip of vegetables?
phrases.notes: Meaning: the corners should get the same status as a ראש תור.

phrases.english: Didn't we learn in a משנה:
If there was a triangular tip of vegetables
poking into another field, it is permitted,
because the end of the field can be seen!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא רֹאשׁ תּוֹר יָרָק? מִי לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה that a person might fill the corners
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Filling the corners should be permitted, just like a ראש תור. If so, there is nothing harmful to make a precaution against.

steps.title: Answer: the triangular-plot leniency does not apply in a small bed
steps.stepSummary: The leniency of ראש תור applies only to large fields. It does not apply in a small ערוגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no 'triangular tip' leniency in a garden bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ראש תור leniency works in big fields, but not in a small garden bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a big field, a triangle-shaped tip is clearly seen as part of a separate field. In a tiny 6x6 bed, the seeds are so close together that no clear border can be seen. So filling the corners would be real כלאים, and רב's precaution stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A small garden bed (here, 6 by 6 טפחים)
There is no (this rule does not apply)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's restriction is a precaution in case the person fills the corners. The ראש תור leniency does not help, because it only works in big fields, not in a small ערוגה.

phrases.english: There is no triangular-tip leniency in a garden bed.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope: the ראש תור rule applies only to large fields.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ראש תור leniency would permit filling the corners of a bed.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a small bed the border cannot be seen, so the leniency does not apply.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה applies even to a bed among other beds
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the משנה's permission to plant five species in a bed applies even when the bed is surrounded by other beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: We learned the משנה even about a garden bed that is among other garden beds.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different view from רב. The משנה's permission applies even to a bed that sits among other planted beds, not only to a bed standing alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was worried about mixing near the edges and corners. שמואל does not limit the משנה that way. In his view, a bed may be surrounded by other beds and the planting is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A garden bed among other garden beds

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
We learned it about a garden bed among garden beds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עֲרוּגָה בֵּין הָעֲרוּגוֹת שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative approach to רב's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's permission applies even to a bed surrounded by other beds.

steps.title: Challenge: won't the seeds of neighboring beds mix?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל can allow this when the plants of neighboring beds would mix together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they become mixed up with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל. If beds sit right next to each other, the plants of one bed will mix with the plants of the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two beds side by side with different species and no gap between them seem to be exactly what כלאים forbids. So how can שמואל permit it?

keyTerms.meaning: They become mixed with each other

phrases.english: But they become mixed up with each other!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a bed among other beds is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Beds right next to each other will have their species mixing, which is כלאים.

steps.title: Answer: the rows face different directions
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that each row is planted in a different direction, so the species look separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he turns one row this way and one row that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rows of neighboring beds are planted facing different directions. Because of this, they do not look mixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one bed's rows run north-south and the next bed's rows run east-west, the eye can tell where one ends and the other begins. A visible difference like this is enough to avoid the appearance of כלאים.

phrases.english: Where he turns one row this way
and one row that way.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case: the rows are angled in different directions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Beds side by side would look mixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rows facing different directions are clearly separate, so it is allowed.

steps.title: A question from ארץ ישראל: does one furrow separate the beds?
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports a question asked in ארץ ישראל: if a person digs one furrow along the whole length between the beds, does that count as a separation?
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: They asked in the West (ארץ ישראל): If he opened one furrow across its whole length, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens here. Does a single furrow running the full length between beds count as a proper separation?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A furrow is a dug-out groove in the ground. The question is whether this small physical gap is enough to keep the species from counting as mixed. This sets up the disagreement in the next steps.

phrases.english: עולא said: They asked in the West:
If he opened one furrow
across its whole length, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about how beds can be separated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a single furrow along the whole length count as a separation between different species?

steps.title: רב ששת: the mixing cancels the furrow
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the mixing of the plants cancels the furrow, so it does not count as a separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The mixing comes and cancels the row.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers strictly. A single furrow does not help, because the plants still mix over it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב ששת's view, the plants grow and mix across the narrow furrow. The mixing 'wins' and makes the furrow meaningless as a border.

phrases.english: רב ששת said:
The mixing comes and cancels the row.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: בָּא עִרְבּוּב וּבִיטֵּל אֶת הַשּׁוּרָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The furrow does not count as a separation, because the mixing cancels it.

steps.title: Second view: the mixing does not cancel the furrow
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion says the mixing does not cancel the row, so a single furrow is a valid separation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: Its mixing does not cancel the row.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא answers leniently. A single furrow is enough to separate the species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of רב ששת. Even if some of the plants touch, the furrow still marks a real border. The next step attacks this lenient view.
steps.confusionAlert: Our text says רב אסי here, but in the next step רבינא challenges רב אשי. Still, the challenge in the next step is aimed at this lenient view.

phrases.english: רב אסי said:
Its mixing does not cancel the row.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי אָמַר: אֵין עֵירוּבוֹ מְבַטֵּל אֶת הַשּׁוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב ששת in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The furrow does count as a separation, because the mixing does not cancel it.

steps.title: רבינא's challenge from single rows of cucumbers, gourds and beans
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the lenient view from a משנה: two rows of each species are allowed, but one row of each is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged רב אשי: One who plants two rows of cucumbers, two rows of gourds, and two rows of Egyptian beans is permitted. One row of cucumbers, one row of gourds, and one row of Egyptian beans is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the lenient view using a משנה. Single rows of different species next to each other are forbidden, even though rows have natural gaps between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a single gap between rows were enough, then single rows should also be permitted. The fact that the משנה forbids single rows suggests that one small separation does not stop the mixing.

phrases.english: רבינא challenged רב אשי:
One who plants two rows of cucumbers,
two rows of gourds,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת שֶׁל פּוֹל הַמִּצְרִי — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: two rows of Egyptian beans: it is permitted.
One row of cucumbers
and one row of gourds

phrases.aramaic: וְשׁוּרָה אַחַת שֶׁל פּוֹל הַמִּצְרִי — אָסוּר!
phrases.english: and one row of Egyptian beans: it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lenient view of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that mixing does not cancel the separating row
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Single rows of different species are forbidden even though there is a gap between them. This suggests one small separation is not enough.

steps.title: Answer: these plants have spreading branches
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that cucumbers, gourds and beans are a special case, because their long branches spread and tangle across the rows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because there are spreading branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The lenient view is defended. That משנה is a special case, because these plants send out long branches that cross into the next row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cucumbers, gourds and beans grow long vines that reach across and tangle together, and this cancels the gap. Ordinary vegetables do not spread like that, so for them a single furrow still works as a separation.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different (marks a special case)

steps.whatToRemember: There is a disagreement about whether one furrow separates species. The lenient view survives רבינא's challenge, because the single-rows משנה deals with vine plants whose branches spread and tangle.

phrases.english: It is different here,
because there are spreading branches.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: vine plants with spreading branches are different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to prove that one separating gap never helps.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition there comes from the tangling branches. Ordinary vegetables can be separated by one furrow.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: how to fill a whole garden with vegetables
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches a method: make a 6x6 bed, plant five circles in it, and fill the corners with whatever you want.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One who wants to fill his whole garden with vegetables makes a bed of six by six, makes five circles in it, and fills its corners with whatever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical teaching. It shows how to use the whole garden for vegetables without breaking כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting each species in a circle keeps it clearly separate from the others. Because the circles are clearly marked, the leftover corners can also be planted. This is how a person can make the most of the space.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical plan for planting a full garden with several species while staying within the laws of כלאים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רב כהנא said that רבי יוחנן said:
One who wants to fill his whole garden with vegetables
makes a bed six by six
and makes five circles in it,
and fills its corners with whatever he wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, practical teaching about using the whole garden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Make a 6x6 bed with five circles of different species, and the corners may be filled with any species.

steps.title: What about the plants between the circles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's method. The spaces between the five circles seem to contain plants that would mix with the circles.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are plants in between the circles!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's 6x6 bed method from Step 12. It points out that whatever grows in the spaces between the circles would touch the circles and cause forbidden mixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's method kept the five circles apart from each other. The problem is the ground in between them. If that ground is planted, those plants border the circles directly, with no separation at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is! (an opening that raises a problem)
in between, the spaces between things

phrases.english: But there are [plants] in between!
phrases.notes: Refers to the spaces between the five circles in the 6x6 bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical workability of רבי יוחנן's method in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's 6x6 bed with five circles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The spaces between the circles would hold plants that touch the circles, so the species would mix and create כלאים.

steps.title: The spaces between are left empty
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי answers that the method works only when the spaces between the circles are left unplanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: this is a case where he leaves the space in between empty.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי answers the challenge from Step 13. רבי יוחנן's method assumes the ground between the circles is left bare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps רבי יוחנן's method exactly as it was. It simply narrows the case: the spaces between the circles are left empty, so nothing grows there to cause mixing. Only the circles themselves and the corners are planted.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי ינאי said

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
[It is a case] where he leaves the space in between barren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the in-between spaces are left empty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole bed, including the spaces between the circles, is planted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the circles and corners are planted. The spaces between them stay bare, so there is no mixing.

steps.title: Plant the spaces between in the opposite direction
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer. The spaces between the circles may be planted, as long as they are sown in the opposite direction from the circles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: if the circles were planted lengthwise, he plants the spaces between widthwise. If the circles were planted widthwise, he plants the spaces between lengthwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second answer to Step 13. The spaces between the circles do not have to stay empty. They only need to be planted in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the school of רבי ינאי, רב אשי lets the whole bed be used. Planting the rows crosswise makes each species look clearly separate, so it does not appear to be one mixed field. The visible change in direction does the work of a separation.

keyTerms.meaning: lengthwise (literally the warp threads of a weave)
widthwise (literally the woof threads of a weave)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is just adding to the school of רבי ינאי. He disagrees with them: they require the spaces between to stay empty, and he allows planting there in a different direction.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ זְרוּעִין שְׁתִי — זוֹרְעָן עֵרֶב,
phrases.english: If [the circles] were planted lengthwise, he plants [the in-between] widthwise;
[if they were planted] widthwise, he plants [the in-between] lengthwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative answer: a change in planting direction counts as a visible separation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spaces between must be left empty, as the school of רבי ינאי said.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spaces between may be planted, as long as the direction is opposite to the circles.

steps.title: רבינא challenges רב אשי: a vegetable needs six handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: רבינא begins a challenge to רב אשי from a ברייתא. It says one vegetable next to another needs a working space of six טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא raised an objection to רב אשי: the work space of one vegetable next to a different vegetable is six handbreadths. And we view them...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's answer from Step 15 by quoting a ברייתא. The quote continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a vegetable needs six טפחים of 'work space' around it when it is next to a different vegetable. That seems to mean a mere change in direction is not enough, and real distance is needed. The words 'and we view them' begin the ברייתא's method of measuring, which finishes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: the work space of a vegetable, the area needed to tend it
and we view them (the start of a measuring method)

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection to Rav Ashi:
The work space of a vegetable next to another vegetable
is six handbreadths.
And one views them
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer in Step 15 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that planting in the opposite direction is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a vegetable needs six טפחים of space from a different vegetable, then plants packed into the spaces of a 6x6 bed are too close. Changing direction alone would not solve the problem.
